summary: Frontend-only retest of the sidebar scrollbar fix in HeadlessChrome 145 at 1920x700, logged in as admin andrei.melek@gmail.com. All checks pass. CSS.supports('selector(::-webkit-scrollbar)') is true. The scrollbar-width/scrollbar-color rules now sit only inside @supports not selector(::-webkit-scrollbar), so they do not apply in Chromium: computed scrollbarWidth and scrollbarColor on nav.sidebar-scroll are both 'auto', in both sidebar states. ::-webkit-scrollbar is 4px x 4px. ::-webkit-scrollbar-button is display:none, 0x0, and a :single-button rule is present. Collapsed sidebar (64px): scrollHeight 1022 > clientHeight 700, wheel scrolled to scrollTop 322, scrollWidth == clientWidth (63). Expanded sidebar (240px): scrollHeight 1069 > clientHeight 700, wheel scrolled to scrollTop 369, scrollWidth == clientWidth (239). The sidebar-collapse-toggle switches 64 <-> 240px. The collapsed tooltip shows 'OPERAȚIONAL / Recepție'. The only console error is the expected 401 from /api/auth/me before login; there are no page errors. The HIGH issue from iteration_18 is resolved.
action_items: Optional cleanup: remove the empty '.sidebar-scroll { }' rule in index.css (line 74).
critical_code_review_comments: The CSS fix is correct: standard scrollbar properties are fenced by @supports not selector(::-webkit-scrollbar), so Chromium 121+ uses the WebKit rules (4px, no arrow buttons) and Firefox gets the thin/transparent fallback.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Sidebar scrollbar bug is verified fixed via the CSS source and computed styles. Headless Chromium uses overlay scrollbars, so arrow-button rendering on Windows cannot be checked with a screenshot. The sidebar collapsed state is persisted in localStorage key 'sidebar-collapsed' (default collapsed).
